strategy.summary: Family-owned grey-iron foundry (120 staff) under acute cash stress: half the shop floor idle, two shifts on short hours, the bank monitoring monthly. The owner, 66, has no successor and is open to a sale. It supplies two A-class volute casings and is the cheaper source on both. On 310011 it holds a 100% quota and prices at should-cost. On 310012 it holds a 60% quota, prices below its own-plant should-cost and well below Brandlhuber. Its current quotes hold 2026 prices flat but ask for 10-day payment, so the real request is cash, not price. Cost drivers (steel, labour) support a modest increase, not a cut. There is little or no price room, and squeezing it risks the health of a supplier we depend on. The value lies in trading faster payment, binding and higher volume (including quota on 310012) and a 24-month commitment for price stability, plus delivery and quality commitments. The FY2024 financials are stale and look better than the 2026 observations.

findings.text: Part 310011: price EUR 180.52 sits only +0.2% above our bottom-up should-cost of EUR 180.19 (no margin, error about 5%). The supplier earns essentially no margin on this part. There is no real room for a price cut; the economic room is in terms (payment, volume, duration), not in price.

Part 310012: price EUR 359.17 is -3.0% below our should-cost of its own plant (EUR 370.21), so it sells below full cost. Against Brandlhuber's plant estimate (EUR 347.27) it is +3.4%, which is within the 5% error band. That comparison shows Brandlhuber's plant is cheaper; it does not show Wimbacher is overpriced. Wimbacher is still 6.7% below Brandlhuber's actual quote of EUR 383.06.

Its cost drivers rose over 12 months and back a modest increase, not a cut. Steel/ferro-alloys (PPI-C241) are +6.5% at a weight of 0.25-0.27, about +1.6-1.8% on price. Labour (LCI-C) is +2.7% at a weight of 0.31, about +0.8%. Power (PPI-D351) is -3.7% at a weight of 0.1, about -0.4%. Net driver pressure is about +2.0-2.2%. The arguments in our favour (steel -6.3% since the 2023-08 peak, power -43.5% since 2022) are not checkable and the steel one is small.

Price history runs against its costs. Both parts were cut by -5.6%, -0.1% and -1.4% (-7.0% since 2023) while steel and labour rose. The current quotes hold the 2026 prices flat but ask for payment in 10 days instead of 30. The real request is cash, not price.

The past RFQs show it is competitive. In 2024, part 310011: its EUR 203.8 against Pfaffenreuth's EUR 204.2. In 2025, part 310012: its EUR 390.2 against Brandlhuber's EUR 385.2, yet it was awarded. Its current prices are 11-13% below those RFQ levels, so a re-tender is unlikely to beat it on price.
Should-cost confidence is only 5% error and the driver weights are category-team estimates. Market news on iron castings (+1.8%) is lower than the steel PPI, which tempers its cost argument somewhat.

findings.text: Wimbacher is under acute liquidity stress, and the managing director is the decision-maker. During our June visit half the shop floor was idle, two shifts were on short hours, and the MD talked mostly about cash and the banks. In the August call he asked twice for earlier payment, said the bank reviews them monthly, and stated 'I cannot sign anything that lowers our margin now.' Expect resistance to price cuts and readiness to trade on cash.

They have repeatedly asked for faster payment: invoices paid within 10 days in exchange for a cash discount (March and June 2026, and again by phone in August). Today's terms are 30 days net against our 60-day standard. Payment days are the cheapest currency we have to swap for price or for no increase.

The formal financial data contradicts the qualitative picture. The FY2024 filing shows a 39.9% equity ratio and a stable credit index of 231. These figures are stale: what we observed in 2026 points to deterioration. For stabilise/secure_supply cases this creates a margin-health risk: pushing price on part 310012, which is already sold about 3% below its own-plant should-cost, could cost us more than it saves.

The 66-year-old owner has no family successor and is open to selling the company. Stable, committed volume raises the company's sale value, so a longer contract or binding volume is worth a lot to him. The flip side is a continuity and change-of-control risk for us.

The sales director said twice (March and September) that they are reviewing small accounts and focusing on customers with volume. Our spend is about 6.7% of their turnover and our forecast volume is rising, so we should be on the protected side of that review. The message still signals that volume is their key ask.

We pay reliably but slightly late: 2.5 days after due on average, 82.4% of invoices late, none more than 10 days late. For a cash-hungry supplier even small delays hurt. Paying on time is a low-cost gesture, but we cannot claim to be a perfect payer.

Their style is cooperative and administrative, with no threats in their correspondence. They plan their year carefully (shutdown from 23 December to 6 January, January call-offs needed by 10 December). Their history shows they accept below full cost to keep volume and settle about 2 percentage points below their ask.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070130 covers both volute casings (310011, 310012), runs 2024-01-01 to 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice, so the deadline to stop renewal is 2026-10-02. That window is still open as of 2026-09, but only for days. Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, i.e. by about 2026-10-02 for 2027. If Wimbacher has not served notice, the 2026 prices (180.52 / 359.17) would roll over.

Commercial terms are payment 30 days net (our standard is 60, so this already favours them), FCA with 45-day standard lead time, and a quality agreement with a 95% OTD target and a EUR 150 flat fee per supplier-caused complaint. The contract has no index clause, no volume commitment and no ppm target.

In three renewals per part Wimbacher has settled about 2.1-2.4 pp below its ask, and every time below its own ask: -2.9 to -5.6, +1.3 to -0.1, +0.9 to -1.4. Prices are down 7% since 2023. On 310011 all four events record 'accepted below full cost to keep the volume'. Both parts move in lockstep, so in practice they are negotiated as a bundle.

Our dependency differs by part. On 310011 Wimbacher holds 100% quota and Pfaffenreuth is qualified but at 0%; its 2024 quote was 13% higher. On 310012 it holds 60% and Brandlhuber is active at 40% at a price 6.7% higher. We own the tooling on both parts, so a move is technically possible. Wimbacher won both periodic benchmark RFQs.

Wimbacher's dependency on us looks high. Our spend is about EUR 1.29M a year, roughly 6.7% of its EUR 19.3M turnover. The file shows signs of cash stress: repeated requests for faster payment, short hours, the MD citing the bank, and an owner seeking a successor. It already sells 310012 about 3% below our should-cost for its plant. Squeezing price further risks supplier health on an A-class casting. The evidence on the category goal is thin.

findings.text: On-time delivery is slipping: rolling OTD against requested date fell from 92.2% (2025Q4) to 82.4% (2026Q3), below the 95% contract target and the 84.6% peer median. Against its own confirmed date it is 88.2%. Avg 11.6 days late when late, max 23.
The lateness sits in part:310012. Its requested-date OTD is 74.1% (25.9% late), against 91.7% for part:310011 over the last 12 months. The second source sup:70110 already holds a 40% quota on 310012.
Quality is improving but still above peers. Rolling ppm dropped from 1379 (2025Q3) and 1290 (2026Q2) to 651 on 4 complaints, against a 457 peer median. No 8D reports are overdue.

Most complaints are on part:310011: 18 QNs, 15 of them supplier-caused, with EUR 1,350 recharged in total. Defects recur: missing marking, wrong material certificate, porosity and leakage. Two recent material-certificate QNs and qn:20005022 were not supplier-caused. Closing 8Ds takes a long time (~2-3 months). part:310012 has had no QN since 2025-07.

Our volume outlook is rising and the forecasts are shared with the supplier. part:310011: 5220 forecast against 5060 ordered in the last 12 months. part:310012: 2010 against 1786. This is valuable to a supplier with idle capacity that is focusing on volume customers.

Prices have fallen 7% since 2023 on both parts. Current prices are 180.52 and 359.17. 310011 sits at should-cost. For 310012, the price is 3% below its own should-cost but 3.4% above the should-cost based on sup:70110's plant. Its rival price is 383.06, so it is already the cheaper source.

arguments.text: We are already the cheapest source on both casings and price at or below our own cost. On 310012 we sit at 359.17 against Brandlhuber's 383.06, about 6% below them, and below the customer's own should-cost estimate for our plant (370.21). On 310011 our 180.52 is at the customer's should-cost (180.19), with no margin at all. There is nothing left to cut.

We have given back 7% over three renewals on both parts (-5.6%, -0.1%, -1.4%), and each time we settled below our own ask. Our records note that on 310011 we accepted these prices below full cost to keep the volume. This year our quote holds prices flat; we are asking for no increase.

Our cost drivers are rising, not falling. Basic iron and steel is up 6.5% in 12 months and labour is up 2.7%; together they weigh about 0.56 of our cost. Iron castings producer prices are +1.8%. A flat price already means we absorb roughly 2-3%.
Delivery and quality have improved. The scorecard has been class A/green for five quarters, ppm fell to 651 in the latest period, and the 310012 ppm over the last 12 months is 0.
Re-tendering would not beat us. In the 2024 benchmark Pfaffenreuth quoted 204.2 against our 203.8, and moving the 310011 tooling costs the customer time and risk.
10-day payment is a fair, normal trade: we offer a cash discount for it, and the customer pays on average 2.5 days late anyway.

weak_points: Our liquidity: the customer saw half the floor idle, short-time shifts, and our MD talking about the bank. They know we need cash and work more than they need us.
The owner has no successor and the company may be sold, which raises a continuity-risk question.
On-time delivery against the requested date is only 74% on 310012 (82% overall last 12 months), below the 95% contract target.
Fifteen supplier-caused QNs on 310011, recurring defects (wrong certificates, missing marking, porosity, leakage) and slow 8D closures.
Electricity is down 3.7% y/y and 43% below 2022, so energy offsets part of the steel story.
Brandlhuber is already qualified on 310012 at 0 ppm and could take quota; Pfaffenreuth is qualified on 310011.
Our FY2024 financials are stale; a current credit check might look worse.
The 90-day notice window under clause 3.1 has effectively passed, so we cannot force a 2027 increase.
wants: Payment in 10 days (we grant 2% skonto) or at least 14-20 days; this is worth more to us than price.
A higher quota on 310012 (from 60% toward 80-100%) to fill idle capacity.
A binding annual volume and a 24-month contract, which help with the bank and the sale value.
In exchange, we hold 2026 prices flat for 2027 and possibly 2028, or give a small step down (around 0.5-1%) only with both fast payment and the quota shift.
A delivery improvement plan and a ppm target are acceptable, but not a higher chargeback per complaint.
red_lines: No price cut on 310012 below current 359.17, which is already below cost.
No cut on 310011 without both 10-day payment and binding volume or quota.
No longer payment terms than 30 days.
No index clause that only goes down (electricity-weighted); steel and labour must count symmetrically.
No chargeback above EUR 150 per complaint and no tooling cost on our side.
red_team.opening: Thank you for the good cooperation. Our scorecard has been green for five quarters, and despite steel +6.5% and labour +2.7% we are holding the 2026 prices unchanged for 2027: 180.52 for 310011 and 359.17 for 310012, still clearly below the alternative source. In return we ask for payment within 10 days, against which we grant a cash discount. We would also welcome talking about a 24-month agreement with committed volume and a larger share of 310012, which would allow us to keep prices stable over the whole term.

rebuttals.answer: We agree that your prices are competitive and we value that; we are not asking you to cut below cost, and our aim is to keep today's prices stable on both casings. On the larger casing we see room to give you more of the volume, and on the smaller one the price already sits on our own estimate, so it covers your cost and calls for no increase.

We recognise the moves you made in past renewals and we appreciate that your quote holds prices flat. We see flat prices as the fair basis too. What we would like to add is what makes them sustainable for you: rising, committed volume and a longer term, rather than a further price change in either direction.

Steel and labour have risen, that is true. Electricity, also part of your cost, has fallen over the same period, so the net effect is smaller than the two rising drivers suggest. Your contract also fixes prices per calendar year with a notice period. Rising forecast volume spreads your fixed costs and offsets part of the remaining pressure.

The improvement is real and we welcome it, especially the lower ppm. On-time delivery against our requested dates is still clearly below the contract target and has slipped compared with a year ago. Rolling ppm also remains above the peer median, which is why we would like to agree delivery and quality commitments alongside a longer contract.

We have no wish to re-tender; we want to build the partnership with you. For completeness, we own the tooling on both casings and further sources are already approved, so continuity is ensured on our side. We would rather put that security into a committed, longer agreement with you.

We have heard your request for faster payment and we take it seriously; we are willing to discuss shorter payment as part of the overall package, with the discount reflected in the agreed price. On punctuality, our payment record is reliable, never far beyond due date, and we are happy to commit to paying strictly on time.

press: We would welcome hearing how you plan to bring on-time delivery on the larger casing up to the contract target, as that would make a larger share easier for us to place with you.
Could we agree a quality target together, so that the recurring certificate and marking issues on the smaller casing stay resolved?
As energy costs have eased, we would see them as balancing part of the steel increase when we look at flat prices.
A longer committed term would give both of us planning security, including through any change in your ownership, and we would be glad to shape it with you.
We would appreciate understanding the cash discount you have in mind, so we can build faster payment into a package that works for both sides.
